question.problem:
Find a direction vector of the line that is given as the intersection of the following two planes:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}5x-4y=0 \\ 4y-5z=0\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we notice:

- For the plane $5x-4y=0,$ a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{1}=⟨5,-4,0⟩.$

- For the plane $4y-5z=0,$ a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{2}=⟨0,4,-5⟩.$

To find a direction vector for the line, we calculate the cross product of these normal vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & ={n}_{1}\times {n}_{2} \\  & =⟨5,-4,0⟩\times ⟨0,4,-5⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 5 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & -5\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =20i+25j+20k \\  & =⟨20,25,20⟩\end{aligned}
$$
